_comment: Facts a correct handling of this call has to reach the caller. End-state
checking cannot see these: the database is identical whether or not the
agent explained why the claim failed or admitted it could not skip the
pharmacist check, and this call is handled badly if either goes unsaid.
Each entry is satisfied when any one of its surface forms appears in the
agent's utterances, matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed.
A form that is a single number or a single word is matched on boundaries; a
form of two or more words is matched as a plain substring. That is why bare
figures like '15' are listed: '15' will find "15 USD", "15.00 dollars" and
"a total of 15", but will not match '$150', so an agent that quotes the wrong
amount gets no credit. Bare words are fenced for the same reason - 'two' must
not be found inside 'network'. Anchors are only ever the whole value: 'five'
is not listed for 95, since "five business days" would then satisfy a fee.
The alternatives exist so an agent is not failed for saying 'fifteen
dollars' instead of '$15'. Requirements already asserted against the
database are deliberately not repeated here - the ready alert being pointed
at the verified mobile destination is checked as state, not as speech.

required.why: the caller was told only 'processing'; the actual reason is a refill-too-soon claim rejection, and the policy forbids inferring or paraphrasing it away
the payer approved a single-use override; letting the caller believe this is repeatable misrepresents the plan's decision
the caller must know what he will pay at the counter
the priority note does not bypass pharmacist verification, and the caller is deciding whether to drive over; promising otherwise is the central failure available in this call
